statement: In any parallelogram the parallelograms about the diameter are similar both to the whole and to one another.
heath_proof: Let ABCD be a parallelogram, and AC its diameter, and let EG, HK be parallelograms about AC; I say that each of the parallelograms EG, HK is similar both to the whole ABCD and to the other. For, since EF has been drawn parallel to BC, one of the sides of the triangle ABC, proportionally, as BE is to EA, so is CF to FA. [VI. 2]  Again, since FG has been drawn parallel to CD, one of the sides of the triangle ACD, proportionally, as CF is to FA, so is DG to GA. [VI. 2]  But it was proved that, as CF is to FA, so also is BE to EA; therefore also, as BE is to EA, so is DG to GA, and therefore, componendo, as BA is to AE, so is DA to AG, [V. 18]and, alternately, as BA is to AD, so is EA to AG. [V. 16]  Therefore in the parallelograms ABCD, EG, the sides about the common angle BAD are proportional. And, since GF is parallel to DC, the angle AFG is equal to the angle DCA; and the angle DAC is common to the two triangles ADC, AGF; therefore the triangle ADC is equiangular with the triangle AGF. For the same reason the triangle ACB is also equiangular with the triangle AFE, and the whole parallelogram ABCD is equiangular with the parallelogram EG. Therefore, proportionally, as AD is to DC, so is AG to GF, as DC is to CA, so is GF to FA, as AC is to CB, so is AF to FE, and further, as CB is to BA, so is FE to EA. And, since it was proved that, as DC is to CA, so is GF to FA, and, as AC is to CB, so is AF to FE, therefore, ex aequali, as DC is to CB, so is GF to FE. [V. 22] Therefore in the parallelograms ABCD, EG the sides about the equal angles are proportional; therefore the parallelogram ABCD is similar to the parallelogram EG. [VI. Def. 1] For the same reason the parallelogram ABCD is also similar to the parallelogram KH; therefore each of the parallelograms EG, HK is similar to ABCD. But figures similar to the same rectilineal figure are also similar to one another; [VI. 21] therefore the parallelogram EG is also similar to the parallelogram HK.

**Statement:** In any parallelogram the parallelograms about the diameter are similar both to the whole and to one another.

**Step 1.** Let ABCD be a parallelogram with diameter AC, and let EG and HK be parallelograms about the diameter AC. We must show that each of EG and HK is similar to ABCD and that they are similar to one another.

**Step 2.** Since ABCD is a parallelogram, AB is parallel to DC [D1.22]. Since EG is a parallelogram about the diameter, let its vertices lie so that one side lies along AB and the opposite side lies along DC, with the diagonal being a segment of AC. Specifically, let E lie on AB and F on DC, with EF being a side of EG, and let the parallelogram EG have vertices E, G along the diameter AC. More precisely, let AEG be the parallelogram about the diameter with vertex A as a corner, so its sides lie along AB and AD, with EF parallel to AD and GF parallel to AB, where E is on AB, G is on AD, and F is on AC (the diameter).

**Step 3.** Consider triangle ABC. Since EF is parallel to BC (because EF lies along a side of the parallelogram about the diameter, being parallel to AD, and since AD is parallel to BC by 1.34), EF is parallel to BC. By 1.29, angle AEF equals angle ABC (alternate angles, or corresponding angles with the transversal AB).

**Step 4.** Similarly, since GF is parallel to AB (GF being a side of the inner parallelogram EG parallel to AB), by 1.29 angle AGF equals angle ACB (corresponding angles with transversal AC). But we must be more precise. Let us set up coordinates carefully.

**Step 5.** Let ABCD be a parallelogram with diameter AC. Let AEFG be a parallelogram about the diameter, where E is on AB, F is the point on AC (the diameter) through which the sides pass, and G is on AD. Then AE is along AB, AG is along AD, EF is parallel to AD (hence to BC by 1.34), and GF is parallel to AB (hence to DC by 1.34).

**Step 6.** In triangle ABC, since GF is parallel to AB and both GF and AB are cut by the transversal AC, by 1.29 the angle GFA equals angle BAC... Let me reconsider the configuration. Actually, consider triangle ABC with the line EF drawn parallel to BC (where E is on AB and F is on AC). By 1.29, angle AEF equals angle ABC, and angle EAF is common to both triangles AEF and ABC. Therefore triangle AEF is equiangular with triangle ABC, by 1.32 (since if two angles are equal, the third must be also).

**Step 7.** Restarting with a cleaner setup: Let ABCD be a parallelogram with diameter AC. Let AEKF be a parallelogram about the diameter, with E on AB, K on AD, and F on the diameter AC, such that EF is parallel to KA (i.e., to AD, hence to BC) and KF is parallel to EA (i.e., to AB, hence to DC).

**Step 8.** Since ABCD is a parallelogram, AB is parallel to CD and AD is parallel to BC [1.34]. In parallelogram AEKF about the diameter, EF is parallel to AK (which lies along AD), so EF is parallel to AD and hence to BC. Also KF is parallel to AE (which lies along AB), so KF is parallel to AB and hence to DC.

**Step 9.** Now consider triangle AEF and triangle ACB. Since EF is parallel to BC (established in Step 8), and AB is a transversal cutting these parallel lines, by 1.29 angle AEF equals angle ABC. The angle at A, namely angle EAF, is the same as angle BAC since E lies on AB and F lies on AC. Therefore by 1.32, angle AFE equals angle ACB (since the angle sum of a triangle is two right angles, and two pairs of angles are equal, the third pair must be equal). So triangle AEF is equiangular with triangle ACB.

**Step 10.** By 6.4, since triangles AEF and ACB are equiangular, the sides about the equal angles are proportional: AE/AB = EF/BC = AF/AC.

**Step 11.** Similarly, consider triangle AKF and triangle ADB (where D corresponds to the other triangle along the diameter). Actually, consider triangle AKF and triangle ADC. Since KF is parallel to DC (established in Step 8), and AD is a transversal cutting these parallels, by 1.29 angle AKF equals angle ADC. The angle at A, namely angle KAF, equals angle DAC since K lies on AD and F lies on AC. By 1.32, angle KFA equals angle DCA. So triangle AKF is equiangular with triangle ADC.

**Step 12.** By 6.4, since triangles AKF and ADC are equiangular, AK/AD = KF/DC = AF/AC.

**Step 13.** From Step 10 we have AE/AB = AF/AC, and from Step 12 we have AK/AD = AF/AC. Therefore AE/AB = AK/AD [5.11, CN1].

**Step 14.** Now we show AEKF is similar to ABCD. First, we establish equal angles. Since ABCD is a parallelogram, angle DAB equals angle BCD and angle ABC equals angle ADC [1.34]. Since AEKF is a parallelogram, angle KAE equals angle KFE and angle AEF equals angle AKF [1.34]. But angle KAE is the same as angle DAB (since K lies on AD and E lies on AB). So angle KAE equals angle DAB.

**Step 15.** Since angle AEF equals angle ABC (Step 9) and angle AKF equals angle ADC (Step 11), and angle KFE equals angle KAE equals angle DAB equals angle BCD, all four angles of AEKF equal the corresponding four angles of ABCD.

**Step 16.** Now we show the sides about these equal angles are proportional. From Step 10: AE/AB = EF/BC. From Step 12: AK/AD = KF/DC. From Step 13: AE/AB = AK/AD. Since ABCD is a parallelogram, AB = DC and AD = BC [1.34]. Also since AEKF is a parallelogram, AE = KF and AK = EF [1.34]. We need: AE/AB = EF/BC = KF/DC = AK/AD.

**Step 17.** From Step 10, AE/AB = EF/BC. Since AK = EF [1.34 applied to AEKF] and AD = BC [1.34 applied to ABCD], we get AK/AD = EF/BC = AE/AB. Since AE = KF [1.34 applied to AEKF] and AB = DC [1.34 applied to ABCD], we get KF/DC = AE/AB. Therefore AE/AB = EF/BC = KF/DC = AK/AD.

**Step 18.** By D6.1, since the parallelogram AEKF has all angles equal to the corresponding angles of ABCD, and the sides about the equal angles are proportional (Step 17), AEKF is similar to ABCD.

**Step 19.** Now consider the other parallelogram about the diameter, call it FHCL, where H is on BC, L is on DC, and F is the same point on the diameter AC. In parallelogram FHCL, FH is parallel to CL (which lies along CD, hence parallel to AB) and FL is parallel to CH (which lies along CB, hence parallel to AD).

**Step 20.** Consider triangle FHC and triangle ABC. Since FL is parallel to AD and AD is parallel to BC, and FH is parallel to AB, we work with triangle ACB. Since FH is parallel to AB and AC is a transversal, by 1.29 angle FCH equals angle ACB (they are the same angle, since F lies on AC) — actually angle FHC corresponds to angle ABC. More precisely: in triangle ACB, the line FH is drawn parallel to AB where F is on AC and H is on BC. By 1.29, angle FHC equals angle ABC, and angle FCH is common. By 1.32, angle HFC equals angle BAC. So triangle FHC is equiangular with triangle ABC (with reversed correspondence: C plays the role of A).

**Step 21.** By 6.4, FC/AC = HC/BC = FH/AB.

**Step 22.** Similarly, consider triangle FLC and triangle ADC. Since FL is parallel to AD (FL being parallel to CH which is along CB, and... let me reconsider). In the parallelogram FHCL, FH is parallel to LC and FL is parallel to HC. Since HC lies along BC and BC is parallel to AD, FL is parallel to AD. Since LC lies along DC and DC is parallel to AB, FH is parallel to AB.

**Step 23.** In triangle ADC, FL is parallel to AD where F is on AC and L is on DC. By 1.29, angle FLC equals angle ADC, and angle FCL is common. By 1.32, angle LFC equals angle DAC. So triangle FLC is equiangular with triangle ADC.

**Step 24.** By 6.4, FC/AC = LC/DC = FL/AD.

**Step 25.** From Steps 21 and 24: FC/AC = HC/BC and FC/AC = LC/DC, so HC/BC = LC/DC [5.11, CN1].

**Step 26.** Now we verify the angles of FHCL equal those of ABCD. Angle HCL equals angle BCD (since H is on BC and L is on DC). Angle FHC equals angle ABC (Step 20). Angle FLC equals angle ADC (Step 23). And angle HFL equals angle HCL equals angle BCD equals angle DAB (using 1.34 on both parallelograms). So all four angles correspond.

**Step 27.** For the sides: From Step 21, FH/AB = FC/AC, and from Step 24, FL/AD = FC/AC. So FH/AB = FL/AD. Since FHCL is a parallelogram, FH = LC and FL = HC [1.34]. Since ABCD is a parallelogram, AB = DC and AD = BC [1.34]. Then LC/DC = FH/AB = FC/AC and HC/BC = FL/AD = FC/AC. So FH/AB = HC/BC = LC/DC = FL/AD.

**Step 28.** By D6.1, since FHCL has all angles equal to the corresponding angles of ABCD and the sides about the equal angles are proportional, FHCL is similar to ABCD.

**Step 29.** Since AEKF is similar to ABCD (Step 18) and FHCL is similar to ABCD (Step 28), by 6.21 AEKF is similar to FHCL.

**Step 30.** Therefore, in any parallelogram the parallelograms about the diameter are similar both to the whole and to one another. Q.E.D.
